description: Somos un equipo multidisciplinario enfocado en analizar y visualizar datos satelitales para el desafío «¡Sea un detective de tendencias del sistema terrestre!». Nuestro objetivo es desarrollar un prototipo interactivo que identifique y muestre patrones de cambios ambientales y climáticos en la Tierra de forma clara e intuitiva. Contamos con un equipo completo para la programación, análisis y presentación del proyecto.
summary:
AGROBL3SSD is an interactive web platform developed for the challenge "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data" of the NASA International Space Apps Challenge.

The project addresses agricultural vulnerability to climate change by integrating open data from the NASA POWER API (temperature, precipitation, humidity, and solar radiation) with the characteristics of local farmers' plots through a web form. Using a backend in Python, FastAPI, and Pandas, the system processes these environmental variables to run a recommendation algorithm that suggests the most suitable crops for each plot.

It's important because it democratizes access to advanced aerospace technology and science, turning complex satellite data into local, accessible recommendations aimed at optimizing agricultural decision-making and promoting food security in the face of climate variability.
details:
AGROBL3SSD is a web application built to help local farmers decide what to plant based on their land's actual conditions and regional climate data. We developed this project for the "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data" challenge at the NASA International Space Apps Challenge.

What does it do and how does it work?

The platform bridges the physical characteristics of a farm plot with NASA's climatological records to recommend the most viable crops. It works in three straightforward steps:

  1. Plot Registration: Farmers access the web app and fill out a simple form with their location, soil type, and local field conditions.
  2. Climate Query: Using the plot's coordinates (latitude and longitude), our backend queries the NASA POWER Daily Point API to retrieve daily records of temperature, precipitation, humidity, and solar radiation.
  3. Data Cross-Referencing & Recommendation: A Python algorithm processes all this environmental and soil data, displaying on screen which crops have the highest probability of thriving under those specific conditions.

What benefits does it have?

  • Complex data in plain language: Producers don't have to interpret raw meteorological tables or dense technical reports; they get direct, practical planting options for their land.
  • Lower planting risk: Helps prevent crop losses caused by selecting varieties that cannot withstand local temperature swings or moisture levels.
  • Zero hardware costs: Because it is a lightweight web platform, any farmer can use it from a smartphone or computer without buying expensive sensors or specialized equipment.

What is the intended impact of the project?

With AGROBL3SSD, we aim to give small and medium-sized farmers access to the same quality of environmental intelligence used by large agricultural enterprises. In the medium term, this empowers local growers to better plan harvest seasons, optimize water usage, and adapt to sudden climate shifts rather than relying solely on guesswork.

Tools, coding languages, hardware, and software used

  • Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and TypeScript to build clean input forms and display clear results.
  • Backend & API: Python paired with FastAPI to handle external requests, and Pydantic to validate incoming data.
  • Data Analysis: Pandas and NumPy to clean and cross-reference climate time-series, along with Jupyter Notebook where we built the database and tested our recommendation algorithm before moving it to production.
  • Data & Infrastructure: NASA POWER API for meteorological data, GitHub for team version control, and a cloud web server for deployment.

How is your project creative?

Traditionally, NASA satellite datasets remain confined to academic research or government reports. Our approach builds a direct bridge: we translate global atmospheric measurements into an immediate, localized answer for the field. Additionally, we combine the empirical knowledge a farmer already holds about their own soil with objective meteorological observations.

What factors did your team consider?

  • Ease of use: We knew a strong algorithm wouldn't matter if the interface was confusing, so we prioritized a short, straightforward form and readable outputs.
  • Data reliability: We chose NASA POWER because it provides free, consistent, and scientifically validated measurements for any coordinate on the map.
  • Response speed: We built the backend with FastAPI and lightweight Python libraries so that querying NASA's servers and calculating crop matches takes only a few seconds.
dataRefs: NASA POWER (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources)
